subject: Post-call: EverStream inference economics & latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Ahmed <samira@everstream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & pricing checkpoints - EverStream

Hi Samira — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick written recap and a couple of asks so we can put a concrete demo/quote together.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + routing, ~75% generate, 25% embeddings for search.
- Peak concurrency: ~60 qps during business hours (US-east).
- Typical prompt lengths: 120-300 input tokens, expected outputs 80-200 tokens.
- Target latency: 95th pct <= 250ms for immediate routing; 99th pct comfort with 500ms.
- Data residency: US only; no PII to leave the VPC.

Budget & volume signals you gave:
- Monthly active conversations: ~2.5M (conservative) to 6M (aggressive).
- Tokens/month (estimate): 150M - 600M (sum of inputs + outputs).
- Budget band you mentioned: $8k - $35k / month (flexible if unit economics play out).

Questions / asks (so we can model unit economics):
1) Do you have an expected % of streaming vs non-streaming responses? (i.e., do you need token-by-token streaming for user-visible experiences or can many responses be returned as a single completed payload?)
2) Are there endpoints where you can tolerate batching (e.g., nightly/rate-limited bulk scoring) vs those that must be low-latency?
3) Any hard SLOs for 99th pct latency or error budgets we should bake into a Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation?

Preliminary economics (very high-level):
- Hosted standard (lowest ops): good for < ~200M tokens/mo; expected unit cost range $150 - $420 per 1M tokens depending on model/quantization and streaming vs non-streaming.
- Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable TPU/GPU pools): recommended if you exceed ~300M tokens/mo or need tighter 95/99 pctl SLOs; approximate blended unit cost $90 - $240 per 1M tokens when fully amortized (depends on instance type and batch size).
- Practical trade: streaming + strict 95th pct latency tends to push you to higher unit cost (less batching, smaller micro-batches). If you can accept a micro-batch window (20-100ms) or prefix caching we can materially cut cost.

Attached: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf (summary bands) and a short notes doc we’ll populate: everstream-demo-notes.docx

Next steps I suggest:
- You reply to the three asks above with any clarifications on streaming and SLOs.
- We schedule a 45-min demo next week focusing on the routing/latency options and a simple cost simulator with your token bands.
- Marissa will draft a 90-day MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones and sample PO language once we validate volumes.

cc Marissa/Neha to add notes and initial numbers.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Ahmed <samira@everstream.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pricing checkpoints - EverStream

Thanks Nikhil — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications inline.

> Do you have an expected % of streaming vs non-streaming responses?
We expect ~80% of responses to be user-facing where streaming improves UX (progressive reveal), 20% are async summaries/batch jobs.

> Are there endpoints where you can tolerate batching?
Yes — nightly summarization and weekly re-embeddings are fine to batch. Real-time routing (the 80%) needs streaming.

> Any hard SLOs?
We need 95th pct <= 250ms for routing and 99th pct <= 550ms. SLA will be required in contract for production path.

Budget: the $8k - $35k range is what procurement will sign off on for a PO this quarter — we can expand the commit if unit economics are justified.

Also, a couple of compliance items: SOC2 Type II report and audit contact (we’ll need to reference during procurement).

Can you send a short model that maps our 150M-600M token bands to likely monthly cost under both Hosted standard and Dedicated reserved? If there are clear breakpoints where Dedicated becomes cheaper, highlight them.

—Samira
VP Product, EverStream

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Ahmed <samira@everstream.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pricing checkpoints - EverStream

Samira — noting the SLOs and streaming ratio. Below is a concise cost mapping that matches what Nikhil summarized; I’ll attach a simple spreadsheet in the drive link.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model selection: mid-size open LLM with quantized FP16 kernels for generation.
- Effective tokens = input + output; use 200 tokens/interaction average for runtime math.
- Streaming penalty: +35% CPU/GPU time vs non-streaming (smaller micro-batches, more frequent kernel flushes).

Cost bands (illustrative):
- 150M tokens/mo:
  - Hosted standard: ~$1,200 - $3,800 (approx $8 - $25 per 1M tokens using lower-end standard model options)
  - Dedicated (small reserved): ~$1,000 - $2,100 (approx $6.6 - $14 / 1M tokens)
- 300M tokens/mo:
  - Hosted standard: ~$2,800 - $8,400 (approx $9 - $28 / 1M tokens)
  - Dedicated (medium reserved): ~$1,900 - $4,200 (approx $6.3 - $14 / 1M tokens)
- 600M tokens/mo:
  - Hosted standard: ~$6,000 - $16,800 (approx $10 - $28 / 1M tokens)
  - Dedicated (large reserved): ~$3,600 - $8,400 (approx $6 - $14 / 1M tokens)

Key callouts:
- If 80% of traffic requires streaming low-latency, the upper bound of Hosted becomes much closer to Dedicated pricing because streaming reduces batching efficiency. Dedicated still wins for predictable throughput but requires a committed monthly spend.
- A helpful hybrid: Dedicated for the routing/critical path + Hosted fallback for burst/edge cases. That preserves 95th/99th SLOs on the critical path while keeping committed spend lower.

I’ll prepare a 1-page MAP and a pricing simulator that you can tweak live in the demo. Nikhil — if you want, I can include a conservative PO template and the SOC2 pointer for their procurement team.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Ahmed <samira@everstream.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pricing checkpoints - EverStream

Morning — adding technical recommendations from the infra side to match SLAs and keep unit cost reasonable.

1) Batching / micro-batching: For the real-time routing path we recommend micro-batches of 8-16 requests with a max coalesce window of 30ms. This typically preserves sub-250ms 95th pct while gaining a 20-30% throughput improvement vs pure single-request mode.
2) Prefix/KV cache: For repeated system prompts or assistant personas, 10-15% token saving is realistic if you can reuse prefixes across sessions; that directly lowers effective token consumption.
3) Streaming mode: implement token streaming only for the first N tokens (progressive reveal) then fall back to completed payloads for the tail to balance UX and cost.
4) Routing policy: route critical routing requests to Dedicated instances (pinned model version) and route lower-priority reads to Hosted pool. Auto-fallback if Dedicated capacity saturated.

I can include these as options in the demo harness so we can toggle micro-batch sizes and show simulated latency vs cost.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
